$comment: Shared protocol fixture. Single source of truth for BOTH parsers: crates/vara-core/src/chat.rs (Rust) and src/lib/protocol.ts (webview). Rust lock: crates/vara-core/tests/protocol_parity.rs; TypeScript lock: tests/protocol.test.ts. Every expectation here is the real output of vara_core::chat (see protocol_parity.rs); the webview must reproduce it byte for byte.

cases.name: plain_no_markers
cases.note: No protocol at all: the text passes through (trimmed, blank lines collapsed).

cases.name: plain_blank_lines_collapsed
cases.note: Delivery tidy-up: runs of blank lines collapse to one and the ends are trimmed.

cases.name: mission_unterminated_first_line_only
cases.note: Unterminated block: only the FIRST LINE after the marker becomes the goal; the lines after it stay in the display text.

cases.name: mission_unterminated_long_ascii_capped_300
cases.note: Unterminated with no newline: the goal is capped at 300 bytes, and the consumed text goes with it.

cases.name: mission_unterminated_long_arabic_byte_cap
cases.note: Unterminated, no newline, multi-byte text: the 300 cap counts BYTES; here byte 300 lands on a character boundary (2 bytes of prefix), so the goal is exactly 300 bytes before trimming.

cases.name: mission_unterminated_multibyte_cap_floors_to_char_boundary
cases.note: Unterminated, no newline, and the 300-byte cap lands INSIDE a character (odd prefix): the pre-fix Rust code panicked here — 'byte index 300 is not a char boundary' — and chat.rs now floors the cap to 299 bytes. protocol.ts floors it identically.

cases.name: sys_open_url
cases.note: Canonical sys block with a URL target.

cases.name: sys_open_path
cases.note: open_path action with a Windows path target.

cases.name: sys_run
cases.note: run action: the command is the target and always needs an approval card in the shell.

cases.name: sys_screenshot_empty_target
cases.note: screenshot with an empty target is normalized to the literal screen.

cases.name: sys_screenshot_missing_target
cases.note: screenshot without a target field is normalized the same way.

cases.name: sys_computer_use
cases.note: computer_use carries a compact JSON sequence as its target.

cases.name: sys_fenced_json
cases.note: Mangled pair (single brackets + {sys_close}) around a ```json fenced body: the fence is tolerated.

cases.name: sys_single_bracket_pair
cases.note: Single-bracket sys pair is a known variant too.

cases.name: sys_unterminated_short
cases.note: Unterminated sys block, no newline, short body: everything after the marker is consumed and the action still parses.

cases.name: sys_unterminated_long_ascii_capped_400
cases.note: Unterminated sys block, no newline: the cap is 400 bytes, so the JSON is cut, the action is dropped and the tail of the line stays in the display text (no marker leaks).

cases.name: sys_three_blocks
cases.note: Three blocks in one reply (the extractor cap) are all extracted and all removed from the display text.

cases.name: sys_invalid_json_dropped
cases.note: Malformed JSON: the block is still removed from the display text and the action is dropped.

cases.name: sys_unknown_action_dropped
cases.note: Valid JSON but an action outside the allow-list (open_url/open_path/run/screenshot/computer_use): dropped, block removed.

cases.name: sys_open_url_empty_target_dropped
cases.note: open_url requires a target: an empty target is dropped, the block is removed. Only screenshot may omit it.

cases.name: mixed_mission_and_sys
cases.note: Mission extraction runs first, then sys extraction — the exact order in src-tauri/src/commands.rs, so both protocols survive in one reply.
